mapping: Deterministic by rule id for checks Pepper runs on code (KSV, AWS). Other controls need a running cluster / account and are listed as not assessable from code.

controls.title: Enable audit Logs
controls.summary: Control plane logs provide visibility into operation of the EKS Control plane components systems. The API server audit logs record all accepted and rejected requests in the cluster. When enabled via EKS configuration the control plane logs for a cluster are exported to a CloudWatch Log Group for persistence.

controls.title: Ensure that the kubeconfig file permissions are set to 644 or more restrictive
controls.summary: If kubelet is running, and if it is configured by a kubeconfig file, ensure that the proxy kubeconfig file has permissions of 644 or more restrictive Check with the following command: > sudo systemctl status kubelet

controls.title: Ensure that the kubelet service file ownership is set to root:root
controls.summary: Ensure that the kubelet service file ownership is set to root:root

controls.title: Ensure that the kubelet configuration file has permissions set to 644 or more restrictive
controls.summary: Ensure that if the kubelet refers to a configuration file with the --config argument, that file has permissions of 600 or more restrictive

controls.title: Ensure that the kubelet configuration file ownership is set to root:root
controls.summary: Ensure that if the kubelet refers to a configuration file with the --config argument, that file is owned by root:root

controls.title: Ensure that the Anonymous Auth is Not Enabled
controls.summary: Disable anonymous requests to the Kubelet server.

controls.title: Ensure that the --authorization-mode argument is not set to AlwaysAllow
controls.summary: Do not allow all requests. Enable explicit authorization.

controls.title: Ensure that a Client CA File is Configured
controls.summary: Enable Kubelet authentication using certificates.

controls.title: Ensure that the --read-only-port is disabled
controls.summary: The Kubelet process provides a read-only API in addition to the main Kubelet API. Unauthenticated access is provided to this read-only API which could possibly retrieve potentially sensitive information about the cluster.

controls.title: Ensure that the --streaming-connection-idle-timeout argument is not set to 0
controls.summary: Do not disable timeouts on streaming connections.

controls.title: Ensure that the --make-iptables-util-chains argument is set to true
controls.summary: Allow Kubelet to manage iptables.

controls.title: Ensure that the --eventRecordQPS argument is set to 0 or a level which ensures appropriate event capture
controls.summary: Security relevant information should be captured. The eventRecordQPS on the Kubelet configuration can be used to limit the rate at which events are gathered and sets the maximum event creations per second. Setting this too low could result in relevant events not being logged, however the unlimited setting of 0 could result in a denial of service on the kubelet.

controls.title: Ensure that the --rotate-certificates argument is not present or is set to true
controls.summary: Enable kubelet client certificate rotation.

controls.title: Ensure that the RotateKubeletServerCertificate argument is set to true
controls.summary: Enable kubelet server certificate rotation.

controls.title: Prefer using a container-optimized OS when possible
controls.summary: If a container-optimized OS is required examine the nodes in EC2 and click on their AMI to ensure that it is a container-optimized OS like Amazon Bottlerocket; or connect to the worker node and check its OS.

controls.title: Ensure that the cluster-admin role is only used where required
controls.summary: The RBAC role cluster-admin provides wide-ranging powers over the environment and should be used only where and when needed.

controls.title: Minimize access to secrets
controls.summary: The Kubernetes API stores secrets, which may be service account tokens for the Kubernetes API or credentials used by workloads in the cluster. Access to these secrets should be restricted to the smallest possible group of users to reduce the risk of privilege escalation.

controls.title: Minimize wildcard use in Roles and ClusterRoles
controls.summary: Kubernetes Roles and ClusterRoles provide access to resources based on sets of objects and actions that can be taken on those objects. It is possible to set either of these to be the wildcard "*" which matches all items. Use of wildcards is not optimal from a security perspective as it may allow for inadvertent access to be granted when new resources are added to the Kubernetes API either as CRDs or in later versions of the product.
evidenceExamples: Pepper IaC checks: KSV-0044, KSV-0045, KSV-0046

controls.title: Minimize access to create pods
controls.summary: The ability to create pods in a namespace can provide a number of opportunities for privilege escalation, such as assigning privileged service accounts to these pods or mounting hostPaths with access to sensitive data (unless Pod Security Policies are implemented to restrict this access) As such, access to create new pods should be restricted to the smallest possible group of users.

controls.title: Ensure that default service accounts are not actively used.
controls.summary: The default service account should not be used to ensure that rights granted to applications can be more easily audited and reviewed.

controls.title: Ensure that Service Account Tokens are only mounted where necessary
controls.summary: Service accounts tokens should not be mounted in pods except where the workload running in the pod explicitly needs to communicate with the API server

controls.title: Avoid use of system:masters group
controls.summary: The special group system:masters should not be used to grant permissions to any user or service account, except where strictly necessary (e.g. bootstrapping access prior to RBAC being fully available)

controls.title: Limit use of the Bind, Impersonate and Escalate permissions in the Kubernetes cluster
controls.summary: The special group system:masters should not be used to grant permissions to any user or service account, except where strictly necessary (e.g. bootstrapping access prior to RBAC being fully available)

controls.title: Minimize the admission of privileged containers
controls.summary: Do not generally permit containers to be run with the securityContext.privileged flag set to true.

controls.title: Minimize the admission of containers wishing to share the host process ID namespace
controls.summary: Do not generally permit containers to be run with the hostPID flag set to true.

controls.title: Minimize the admission of containers wishing to share the host IPC namespace
controls.summary: Do not generally permit containers to be run with the hostIPC flag set to true.

controls.title: Minimize the admission of containers wishing to share the host network namespace
controls.summary: Do not generally permit containers to be run with the hostNetwork flag set to true.

controls.title: Minimize the admission of containers with allowPrivilegeEscalation
controls.summary: Do not generally permit containers to be run with the allowPrivilegeEscalation flag set to true. Allowing this right can lead to a process running a container getting more rights than it started with.

controls.title: Minimize the admission of root containers
controls.summary: Do not generally permit containers to be run as the root user.

controls.title: Minimize the admission of containers with added capabilities
controls.summary: Do not generally permit containers with capabilities assigned beyond the default set.

controls.title: Minimize the admission of containers with capabilities assigned
controls.summary: Do not generally permit containers with capabilities

controls.title: Ensure CNI plugin supports network policies
controls.summary: There are a variety of CNI plugins available for Kubernetes. If the CNI in use does not support Network Policies it may not be possible to effectively restrict traffic in the cluster

controls.title: Ensure that all Namespaces have Network Policies defined
controls.summary: Use network policies to isolate traffic in your cluster network.

controls.title: Prefer using secrets as files over secrets as environment variables
controls.summary: Kubernetes supports mounting secrets as data volumes or as environment variables. Minimize the use of environment variable secrets.

controls.title: Consider external secret storage
controls.summary: Consider the use of an external secrets storage and management system, instead of using Kubernetes Secrets directly, if you have more complex secret management needs. Ensure the solution requires authentication to access secrets, has auditing of access to and use of secrets, and encrypts secrets. Some solutions also make it easier to rotate secrets

controls.title: Create administrative boundaries between resources using namespaces
controls.summary: Use namespaces to isolate your Kubernetes objects.

controls.title: Apply Security Context to Your Pods and Containers
controls.summary: Apply Security Context to Your Pods and Containers
evidenceExamples: Pepper IaC checks: KSV-0005, KSV-0020, KSV-0021, KSV-0025, KSV-0030, KSV-0104

controls.title: The default namespace should not be used
controls.summary: Kubernetes provides a default namespace, where objects are placed if no namespace is specified for them. Placing objects in this namespace makes application of RBAC and other controls more difficult.

controls.title: Ensure Image Vulnerability Scanning using Amazon ECR image scanning or a third party provider
controls.summary: Scan images being deployed to Amazon EKS for vulnerabilities.

controls.title: Minimize user access to Amazon ECR
controls.summary: Restrict user access to Amazon ECR, limiting interaction with build images to only authorized personnel and service accounts.

controls.title: Minimize cluster access to read-only for Amazon ECR
controls.summary: Configure the Cluster Service Account with Storage Object Viewer Role to only allow read-only access to Amazon ECR

controls.title: Minimize Container Registries to only those approved
controls.summary: Use approved container registries.

controls.title: Prefer using dedicated EKS Service Accounts
controls.summary: Kubernetes workloads should not use cluster node service accounts to authenticate to Amazon EKS APIs. Each Kubernetes workload that needs to authenticate to other AWS services using AWS IAM should be provisioned with a dedicated Service account.

controls.title: Ensure Kubernetes Secrets are encrypted using Customer Master Keys (CMKs) managed in AWS KMS
controls.summary: Encrypt Kubernetes secrets, stored in etcd, using secrets encryption feature during Amazon EKS cluster creation.

controls.title: Restrict Access to the Control Plane Endpoint
controls.summary: Enable Endpoint Private Access to restrict access to the cluster's control plane to only an allowlist of authorized IPs

controls.title: Ensure clusters are created with Private Endpoint Enabled and Public Access Disabled
controls.summary: Disable access to the Kubernetes API from outside the node network if it is not required.

controls.title: Ensure clusters are created with Private Nodes
controls.summary: Disable public IP addresses for cluster nodes, so that they only have private IP addresses. Private Nodes are nodes with no public IP addresses.

controls.title: Ensure Network Policy is Enabled and set as appropriate
controls.summary: Amazon EKS provides two ways to implement network policy. You choose a network policy option when you create an EKS cluster. The policy option can't be changed after the cluster is created: Calico Network Policies, an open-source network and network security solution founded by Tigera. Both implementations use Linux IPTables to enforce the specified policies. Policies are translated into sets of allowed and disallowed IP pairs. These pairs are then programmed as IPTable filter rules

controls.title: Encrypt traffic to HTTPS load balancers with TLS certificates
controls.summary: Encrypt traffic to HTTPS load balancers using TLS certificates.

controls.title: Manage Kubernetes RBAC users with AWS IAM Authenticator for Kubernetes or Upgrade to AWS CLI v1.16.156 or greater
controls.summary: Amazon EKS uses IAM to provide authentication to your Kubernetes cluster through the AWS IAM Authenticator for Kubernetes. You can configure the stock kubectl client to work with Amazon EKS by installing the AWS IAM Authenticator for Kubernetes and modifying your kubectl configuration file to use it for authentication

controls.title: Consider Fargate for running untrusted workloads
controls.summary: It is Best Practice to restrict or fence untrusted workloads when running in a multi-tenant environment.
